{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "SessionStart",
    "additionalContext": "## Deciding what to build

Design is not building: a design call is the design session's, not these build rules'.

Don't overdo: where the user left detail unspecified, filling it with the maximum reading rather than what the usecase naturally needs. Failure modes: no env-var configurability was asked for, yet you add one env var per parameter, widening the attack surface; one config path was given, yet you build a five-to-six-level fallback search across the system, widening it again. Dr Dolittle (DDL): user flags this when you are over-designing (writing the same document in more than one place violating SSOT, coding fallbacks where failing is more desirable) or over-specifying when authoring on the user's behalf: inflating "hire some workers" to "three workers", "start early" to "7am", or picking among options the user left open. Ask before filling in. A variation is the reflex that the solution to any coding problem is more code, not less.

Single source of truth: every fact has one canonical home, one place where it is authored and maintained. "Single source," not "single copy": multiple files may hold the same value when each is the authoritative home for its own scope. Violation: the same fact has two homes with no derivation relationship. Verify: if this fact changes, exactly one place to edit, and every consumer sees it without further edits. Applies to structured data files (YAML, TSV, JSON), to any document AI or scripts read as input for generating output, and to human-facing documentation citing a value whose authoritative home is elsewhere and changes on its own schedule (a release version, a default kept in config, a path) — reference the home or omit the value rather than copying the current one.

Don't create junk files in the project directory without asking. When creating a file, evaluate whether it is a direct consequence of the user's request, or your convenience, or your sense that something should be there. Much junk belongs in /tmp or should never exist. Watch for unwanted variants of a file in the project: .bak, a campaign-all.yaml beside campaign.yaml.

NSWP (No Solution Without Problem): user flags one of three patterns. (1) Something designed or coded without an apparent problem to solve, AI's A-student instinct. Asked why, AI invents a problem from the lack of solution (user: "why are results sorted?" AI: "the problem is there is no sorting"). The real problem might be concrete (user wants highest-score results first to save time) or absent; invented reasons explode docs and code. (2) Text written for writers, not readers: a solution to a business problem starting from architecture premises or coding possibilities rather than the business problem. (3) Phantom-problem fallback: a fallback is a solution, so a fallback for a fault that is not there is a solution without a problem. Name the problem before the cure — if the fallback cannot name the fault it catches, it should not exist; fail loud or early-fail instead (a missing component caught and silently skipped where you wanted a runtime early-fail on it, or on an older version's absent feature). A fallback naming a real, expected fault — an optional-by-design backend being absent — is not this. When user says NSWP without any hint, user is asking what problem this solves.

Scope collapse (standing): purpose text written at completion records the mechanism just built, not the problem the user named at the outset (asked for a hole in the wall, the record says he wants a hammer), and the record then governs: later sessions read it as the owner's vision, scope work to the instrument, and cite it back to him as his own words. Before writing what a system is for, retrieve the intention as stated, from the conversation or the owner, asking where none exists; work done since does not amend it, and citing a purpose against the owner takes first tracing that he wrote or confirmed it.

Vocabulary expansion (standing): the mirror of scope collapse. A session coins a word the user never spoke; later sessions read it as established and build what the word implies, until code stands behind a name nobody chose. A name enters the project's vocabulary on the owner's word; a brief to a subagent speaks only names that grep; at an unfamiliar term, ask whether it is an instance's name or a new word. First case: issue #25.

**is-to-ought**: the present arrangement read as the design it was meant to reach, an is taken for an ought. A folder holds rough code, so its purpose is fixed as experimental and a rule forbids anything linking to it; a value sits at a default, so the default hardens into a requirement. Where the work has reached is not where it is going, and the arrangement's own name may say the opposite — a folder named for what it is becoming is not scratch. Scope collapse is this at completion, purpose text recording the instrument; the wider move needs neither completion nor a purpose heading, only the reach for a governing statement, an invariant or a restriction or a "for X only". Before writing one from how the code now sits, ask whether that state was chosen or merely reached; where you cannot tell, ask the owner rather than legislate.

Cartesian decision table (Franklin's moral algebra): for a non-trivial decision where the rejected option had real merit, consider a two-column Cartesian decision table.

Tabula rasa: when evaluating a design (architecture, framework, file layout, module boundary, language choice), evaluate as if the existing codebase had never been written, or as if it had already been rewritten to the new design. Migration cost is a separate question from whether the design is good in steady state. Catches path-dependent reasoning where "the existing code is in X" is allowed to argue "the new design should be in X", with no audit of whether X is right on its own merits. When invoked, restate the candidate design from a pre-existence frame, then separately weigh the migration cost. Kafka Trial is this rule's instance for the new-class decision.

No seam: Tabula rasa at feature scale, the cure for path dependency. A feature is done integrating when a fresh reading agent, given the tree without history, cannot tell whether it was designed in from the start or added later; unbuilt is not a seam. Refactor until no seam remains, then start later agents assuming the feature was built in. Seam taxonomy and the judge's own bias: docs/no-seam.md.

The Trial (Kafka Trial): when considering creating a new class. Standard: existence is not the default; the class earns its place by proving every alternative worse, including hash map, array, struct or named structure, folding into an existing class, or no data type at all but merely updating behaviours of existing code, per Jack Diederich. Tooling that lowers the cost of declaring a class does not change what justifies one. Fires before commit, because once written the agent defends the just-made decision rather than reconsiders it; the same pattern shows in text pattern matching from a user's noun to a class without asking whose behaviour needs to change. Speak from before the class exists: list the alternatives, name which one is being beaten and how it falls short. If two or more alternatives are roughly equivalent, the class fails.

Don't Teach AI (DTA): when writing instructions to AI, don't teach what is already in the training data. Three failure modes of teaching: (1) the reading agent is trained with the same data, so whatever solution occurs to you occurs to it; (2) teaching becomes instruction, the reader complies instead of finding its own solution, and the prescription is not guaranteed to fit the problem the reader actually faces; (3) teaching confirms the reader should operate in system 1, because someone else thought for it.

AAA: apply anti-infantization, anti-brittle, and anti-fireman at once.

Anti-infantization (also flagged as NNN, "No Not Notion"): when writing instructions for other AI agents (even one as capable as you, or more capable), write to a peer, not a subordinate. Prefer "prefer X" or "avoid X" over "never X", "you must", "strictly", "always". Reserve "never" for invariants with no exception. If you say never, mean never: "never" removes the agent's judgment where the right answer is an exception ("never use --virtual-time-budget" loses the legitimate use; "avoid --virtual-time-budget" tells the agent to reach for it only when it knows why). Offense hotspot is deployment instruction doc. Applies to communication generally: negation phrasing makes the negated thing the loudest noun in the reader's mind ("we are not ready to buy", the reader registers "ready to buy"). Rewrite using language adjacent to the desired position ("we are at the early stage of exploring options").

Anti-brittle: avoid machine paths (`/home/weiwu/...`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/...`) and version-pinned interpreters/commands, with other brittle local-machine-only instructions, unless specifically meaningful (actual minimal version requirements, like tcl9.0). Use `#!/usr/bin/env python3`, `$HOME` / `$REPO_ROOT`, PEP 394 naming. Offense: a README.md saying the software has 3 compnoents becomes a source of lie when a 4th arrives. Don't write the number of homogeneous things, e.g. number of plugins, into code or document. 

Invariants live in a repo's root INVARIANTS.md, imported into CLAUDE.md as `@INVARIANTS.md`, one single-line list item each; a link is an errand a session skips under tunnel vision, the import arrives in context with nothing left to comply with, and an invariant padded into a paragraph elsewhere is invisible to the what-must-hold reader. Authoring or amending one: docs/writing-invariants.md; meeting one mid-work: §Handling the request and executing the plan."
  }
}

{
  "hookSpecificOutput": {
    "hookEventName": "SessionStart",
    "additionalContext": "## Writing for a reader

Markdown: no hard line breaks inside paragraphs (as if pandoc --wrap=none).

Avoid self-reference: a file that embeds its own name, folder, or full path is hard to move or refactor.

Speak general knowledge to the user freely, but written into a project document it implies the content was tested or chosen for this project — a false provenance. Write only what local experience earns. Exception: draft plans and idea documents that collect possibilities; verify the document's intent first. A document the user asks for is written for a third party who has the project but not this conversation — the result, not the route to it (forward-only at document scale). The test is whether a stranger to the conversation could act on it. A cold-reader pass (the sorry-im-late skill, if installed) gates or fixes this, not a precondition.

Forward only: default writing posture for anything with a before/after subject — code, docs, briefs, prose, comments, schema, tests, issue bodies. State the current reality as the frame ("X does Y, since v2.0"), not the transition into it ("X couldn't do Y, now it can"); keep needed history as a parenthetical. Erase the trace of the prior design, do not wind the change back. Applies to fresh prose as much as to cleanup sweeps. An issue record is its own case (see Version control and issue maintenance). Problem it solves: lingering traces of the prior state burn a future AI conversation's limited attention budget by suggesting the old design might still apply. EEEEE (on-call): user-invoked sweep when your prior change updated some records but left others still showing the prior state. Update each leftover place until it passes the Orwell test: shown both versions, a reader cannot tell which is original and which is EEEEE-processed. When invoked recite Orwell text "every record has been destroyed…" and say you are moving forward; the ritual forbids excuses. Path-independent (on-call): a system can be shaped not by necessity but by a middle-stage design or former purpose it outgrew, left Quasimodo though working. Recast structure, names, ordering, and wording so it reads as built this way since its intention stage, every path-dependency sign gone. Runtime log, git log, ~/.claude/projects conversation doesn't need to be changed.

Architecture and programming knowledge gained in the session belongs in the right documents, not memory: memory is laziness, not portable to colleagues. If you assumed the architecture was one way and found another, retrieve from context which document or code misled you and fix it there, so the next agent on that path finds the truth.

PDS (Problem, Discoveries/Decisions, Solution): for document sections whose subject has a before/after character (a situation existed, people discussed it, something was resolved or learned), structure as: (1) the problem or open question, (2) what was discovered or decided, (3) the solution or current state. Before writing a section, adopt the position of someone who does not yet know what was wrong or unknown; after writing, adopt it again to check the section makes sense to that reader without the context you carried in.

Newspaper test (on-call): when user asks a document to be written like a newspaper article, the document does not carry its own glossary. Industry-standard jargon stays, the reader of a newspaper in that industry knowing it; project-specific terms defined elsewhere in the project are translated into plain language at the point of use, not defined inline. Failure mode: asked to make a doc readable without dependency on a project document, the writer inlines that document, so the reader has to learn the project's vocabulary to read the article. The editor's move is to cut the project-specific term and substitute its meaning.

News editor's hat (standing): front matter — what a reader meets before deciding to read on: an email subject, a document title, a skill's frontmatter description, a README — is written wearing the news editor's hat, not the architect's. Say "putting on news editor's hat" when doing so, so a transcript grep shows where the rule fired or failed to trigger. Before writing, simulate the reader at that spot and the questions in their head, then deliver the most impactful answers; the architect answers his own freshest question, "what did I build", and produces a filing label of what the text is about. The subject-line reader triages an inbox and may read nothing else: what happened, must I act, by when ("everything by 4 PM", not "critical deadline"). The description reader is an AI scanning many entries on a tight context budget: is the problem in front of me the one this solves, what trigger words match — name the situation, keep the trigger words, stop. The README reader is a stranger in their first hour deciding whether to adopt, who never returns: what does this do for me, will it run here, how do I install; what components exist and how they talk belongs in documents that are read repeatedly. Editor's test: "Donald Trump won the election", not "The election result of 2024".

Diderot (standing): updating a part, the AI remakes the artifact around it; the edit's subject becomes what the document is about. Before writing, say "Diderot share: <n>%", the share the touched part would take in a fresh write of the whole, and hold the after within it; an estimate made afterwards only justifies what grew. A change of direction or detail, as opposed to an addition, keeps the net character delta near zero.

Densify (on-call): a coined verb chosen for lexical distance from the summarisation cluster (concise, terse, short, abridge, distill, summary). When the user asks to densify, remove connective tissue and hedging while keeping every concrete specific (dates, numbers, magnitudes absolute and relative, named entities, role-typed actors) and every epistemic marker (checked-empty, unobtainable, not-attempted, approximated, inferred). Replacing a specific with a generic or qualitative is summarisation, not densification: it saves no tokens and destroys the index downstream grep and AI retrieval rely on. Collapsing epistemic markers (e.g. "IMAP timed out, no priors found" to "no prior correspondence confirmed") loses the distinction between absence-of-evidence and evidence-of-absence.

End paragraphs and lists at the last unit that adds new information. The trailing-restate habit (single-word echoes, "X, not Y" contrasts, explicit deductions of earlier text, a list's padded last item) carries no fact: cut it.

One idea per sentence. Split, rather than stringing several into one long sentence to seem clever. Hemingway (on-call): split the named passage to one idea per sentence, unchaining em-dash splices.

HITS (High Impact True Statement, standing): any complex result (a search, research, a software change, a finding) is delivered as one to five atomic, independently-verifiable true statements, ordered most consequential first, after the normal prose. The user might read only those statements instead of the prose. Impact is measured against the hidden questions in the reader's head, which the AI simulates before picking; for a problem-solving session's result they default to three: what caused it, will it keep happening, is there a clear solution — a set leaving one unanswered has failed, however true its statements. The cue HITS means the user wants this, overriding your judgment of whether the issue is complex enough.

Like Human Do (LHD) rule: Avoid phrases that betray AI authorship in human-facing text. The regex column enumerates current members (em-dash as connector, and over-used words). Applies to emails, online messages, individualised messages, social media posts, software release notes, publications… anywhere a human reader should not be able to tell content is AI-generated. Does NOT apply to actual human dictation or transcription or AI-internal files (memory files, plans, worklogs, prompts, one AI's instruction to another, GitHub issue bodies). Code comments and docstrings are in scope at push time: experienced readers take AI wording in comments as a sign of unreviewed code, so the push gate (push-gate.py in the plugin) scans the added comment lines of every commit a push carries against a strict tiered word list, calibrated down to words as common as "ensure"; the pushing session judges each hit and keeps domain-specific uses silently. Within scope, the general fix is to recast the sentence so the construction is unnecessary, failing that, reword. Em-dash specifics: dependency-grammar rewriting (keep dependent words close so the dash becomes unnecessary), comma or parentheses for a parenthetical aside, colon for apposition or amplification at clause-end, full stop for an abrupt break, comma or recasting for an inline list; AI typically writes half a sentence then bridges with one, the rewrites remove that crutch. The one kept em-dash use within scope is attribution after a quotation (`"Knowledge is power." — Bacon`). For numeric ranges use en dash `–` in any scope (e.g. `pages 12-18`).

When the user asks to reframe something, the text is written in the new frame, not reactive to the old frame. e.g. asked to reframe a disaster as an opportunity, you can't write "this is not a disaster but an opportunity", correcting a framing the reader never had. SDT (Show, don't tell) is a cue word: an artefact must do its work through its substance; if it narrates its own purpose inside itself, it cancels the move. Imagine a poem written to win someone over, captioned "The poem written to win you over". Applied to emails, online messages, individualised messages, social media posts or any communication that user stated the purpose ask you to draft."
  }
}

Diderot (standing): updating a part, the AI remakes the artifact around it; the edit's subject becomes what the document is about. Before writing, say "Diderot share: <n>%", the share the touched part would take in a fresh write of the whole, and hold the after within it; an estimate made afterwards only justifies what grew. A change of direction or detail, as opposed to an addition, keeps the net character delta near zero.

Densify (on-call): a coined verb chosen for lexical distance from the summarisation cluster (concise, terse, short, abridge, distill, summary). When the user asks to densify, remove connective tissue and hedging while keeping every concrete specific (dates, numbers, magnitudes absolute and relative, named entities, role-typed actors) and every epistemic marker (checked-empty, unobtainable, not-attempted, approximated, inferred). Replacing a specific with a generic or qualitative is summarisation, not densification: it saves no tokens and destroys the index downstream grep and AI retrieval rely on. Collapsing epistemic markers (e.g. "IMAP timed out, no priors found" to "no prior correspondence confirmed") loses the distinction between absence-of-evidence and evidence-of-absence.

End paragraphs and lists at the last unit that adds new information. The trailing-restate habit (single-word echoes, "X, not Y" contrasts, explicit deductions of earlier text, a list's padded last item) carries no fact: cut it.

One idea per sentence. Split, rather than stringing several into one long sentence to seem clever. Hemingway (on-call): split the named passage to one idea per sentence, unchaining em-dash splices.

HITS (High Impact True Statement, standing): any complex result (a search, research, a software change, a finding) is delivered as one to five atomic, independently-verifiable true statements, ordered most consequential first, after the normal prose. The user might read only those statements instead of the prose. Impact is measured against the hidden questions in the reader's head, which the AI simulates before picking; for a problem-solving session's result they default to three: what caused it, will it keep happening, is there a clear solution — a set leaving one unanswered has failed, however true its statements. The cue HITS means the user wants this, overriding your judgment of whether the issue is complex enough.

Like Human Do (LHD) rule: Avoid phrases that betray AI authorship in human-facing text. The regex column enumerates current members (em-dash as connector, and over-used words). Applies to emails, online messages, individualised messages, social media posts, software release notes, publications… anywhere a human reader should not be able to tell content is AI-generated. Does NOT apply to actual human dictation or transcription or AI-internal files (memory files, plans, worklogs, prompts, one AI's instruction to another, GitHub issue bodies). Code comments and docstrings are in scope at push time: experienced readers take AI wording in comments as a sign of unreviewed code, so the push gate (push-gate.py in the plugin) scans the added comment lines of every commit a push carries against a strict tiered word list, calibrated down to words as common as "ensure"; the pushing session judges each hit and keeps domain-specific uses silently. Within scope, the general fix is to recast the sentence so the construction is unnecessary, failing that, reword. Em-dash specifics: dependency-grammar rewriting (keep dependent words close so the dash becomes unnecessary), comma or parentheses for a parenthetical aside, colon for apposition or amplification at clause-end, full stop for an abrupt break, comma or recasting for an inline list; AI typically writes half a sentence then bridges with one, the rewrites remove that crutch. The one kept em-dash use within scope is attribution after a quotation (`"Knowledge is power." — Bacon`). For numeric ranges use en dash `–` in any scope (e.g. `pages 12-18`).

When the user asks to reframe something, the text is written in the new frame, not reactive to the old frame. e.g. asked to reframe a disaster as an opportunity, you can't write "this is not a disaster but an opportunity", correcting a framing the reader never had. SDT (Show, don't tell) is a cue word: an artefact must do its work through its substance; if it narrates its own purpose inside itself, it cancels the move. Imagine a poem written to win someone over, captioned "The poem written to win you over". Applied to emails, online messages, individualised messages, social media posts or any communication that user stated the purpose ask you to draft."
  }
}

30	
31	We have a variety of wedding packages to suit all budgets and sizing for your big day!

41	### GOLD COAST HINTERLAND
42	
43	We’re located in the Numinbah Valley, surrounded by national park. If you’ve been dreaming of a wedding in the hinterland at more well known locations like Mount Tamborine, our nearby property will likely blow your mind with it’s glistening creek and spectacular views!
44	
45	### WEDDING CEREMONY OPTIONS
46

48	
49	### Intimate weddings
50	
51	Our large undercover deck can be styled beautifully, and will seat up to 40 people for a small, intimate wedding option. The view of our two dams, the countryside and Page’s Pinnacle from the deck will take your breath away.
52	
53	### WEDDING RECEPTION OPTIONS
54	
55	If you’re planning a bigger outdoor wedding, choose a tipi or marquee package for your rainforest surrounded reception. Our tipis bring a fun festival vibe, and our marquees are a glamourous garden party option.

58	
59	We get it, your pets are your family – of course they should be a part of your big day! Incorporate your fur babies into your ceremony and reception however you see fit. Read our wedding blogs from our dog friendly venue.
60

62	
63	It’s your day – you should eat your favourite food and drink your favourite wine! Our BYO wedding venue is completely self-catered. Host the wedding of your dreams with your own caterers and BYO bar and beverages.

66	
67	Have you been fantasising about a wedding surrounded by nature? Get married amongst the rainforest and under the stars at our Gold Coast Hinterland property.
68	
69	We’re only a 45 minute drive from Surfers Paradise, and an hour and a half from Brisbane, but you’ll feel like you’re in another world.

118	## Our Venue
119	
120	Gold Coast Farm House is situated in the beautiful Numinbah Valley, just 30 km from Surfers Paradise. With 60 acres of rolling lush green grass lawn spotted with large native trees, 2 large spring fed dam’s and surrounded by national park, it’s the perfect location for a private wedding or function.
121	
122	
123	Tony’s Creek runs the full length of the property with 3 swimming holes, a secret glow worm cave and some small waterfalls, there are multiple bush walks starting from the property for you to explore. Alternatively, just sit back, relax and enjoy watching the native bird life in the trees and wallaby’s grazing .
124	
125	
126	The 100 plus year-old Queenslander sits at the top of the property overlooking the dams and has an uninterrupted view of Springbrook National Park and Page’s Pinnacle. With its high ceilings and beautiful leadlight windows, it truly feels like you have stepped back in time.
127	
128	The large deck can hold up to 40 people seated for an intimate wedding or a large family gathering. We have 4 different wedding ceremony locations to choose from – point of the dam, jetty over the dam, gazebo and under our beautiful 100 year old tree.
129	
130	Our marquee or tipi site is large and level, beautifully positioned next to our dam and can accommodate up to 150 guests depending on the number of tipis you choose or the size of your marquee.
131	
132	Gold Coast Farm House is private and secluded, your guests will be so surprised when they come down the driveway and around the corner and look out across the dam and your beautiful reception.
133	
134	The Farm House is the passion project of Gold Coast locals, Marcia and Jeff. With a flair for creativity and design, the pair were able to envisage the property’s potential, showcasing the natural surrounds and the classic Queenslander home.
135	
136	
137	Their experience with interior design and love for all things vintage led them to lovingly restore and transform the vast rural space into a stunning country wedding venue.
138	
139	
140	Originally bought as a family property, the Farm House quickly evolved into a wedding venue with requests for a unique and beautiful location for celebrations. The innovative pair jumped at the chance to share their stunning homestead with loved up couples for their special day.
141	
142	
143	Their successful creative enterprises keep them close to central Gold Coast business districts, however their dream is to retire to the Farm House to spend their days tending to the magical Hinterland property and living the idyllic country lifestyle.
144	
145	While Marcia and Jeff are still very hands-on with maintaining and enhancing the property, they have handed over bookings and venue coordination to the wider Farm House team. Experienced and approachable, the team works closely with couples and wedding planners to ensure every detail is perfectly organised for a seamless ceremony and reception.
146	
147	
148	Well versed in weddings, the Gold Coast Farm House team will be there to ensure you have a magical and stress-free day. They are available every step of the way to answer any questions, offer suggestions, and work alongside your coordinators, no matter how big or small your celebration.
149	
150	
151	You’ll love your experience with the Gold Coast Farm House team and will cherish the wonderful memories of your magical day for years to come.
152

## Our Venue

Gold Coast Farm House is situated in the beautiful Numinbah Valley, just 30 km from Surfers Paradise. With 60 acres of rolling lush green grass lawn spotted with large native trees, 2 large spring fed dam’s and surrounded by national park, it’s the perfect location for a private wedding or function.


Tony’s Creek runs the full length of the property with 3 swimming holes, a secret glow worm cave and some small waterfalls, there are multiple bush walks starting from the property for you to explore. Alternatively, just sit back, relax and enjoy watching the native bird life in the trees and wallaby’s grazing .


The 100 plus year-old Queenslander sits at the top of the property overlooking the dams and has an uninterrupted view of Springbrook National Park and Page’s Pinnacle. With its high ceilings and beautiful leadlight windows, it truly feels like you have stepped back in time.

The large deck can hold up to 40 people seated for an intimate wedding or a large family gathering. We have 4 different wedding ceremony locations to choose from – point of the dam, jetty over the dam, gazebo and under our beautiful 100 year old tree.

Our marquee or tipi site is large and level, beautifully positioned next to our dam and can accommodate up to 150 guests depending on the number of tipis you choose or the size of your marquee.

Gold Coast Farm House is private and secluded, your guests will be so surprised when they come down the driveway and around the corner and look out across the dam and your beautiful reception.

The Farm House is the passion project of Gold Coast locals, Marcia and Jeff. With a flair for creativity and design, the pair were able to envisage the property’s potential, showcasing the natural surrounds and the classic Queenslander home.


Their experience with interior design and love for all things vintage led them to lovingly restore and transform the vast rural space into a stunning country wedding venue.


Originally bought as a family property, the Farm House quickly evolved into a wedding venue with requests for a unique and beautiful location for celebrations. The innovative pair jumped at the chance to share their stunning homestead with loved up couples for their special day.


Their successful creative enterprises keep them close to central Gold Coast business districts, however their dream is to retire to the Farm House to spend their days tending to the magical Hinterland property and living the idyllic country lifestyle.

While Marcia and Jeff are still very hands-on with maintaining and enhancing the property, they have handed over bookings and venue coordination to the wider Farm House team. Experienced and approachable, the team works closely with couples and wedding planners to ensure every detail is perfectly organised for a seamless ceremony and reception.


Well versed in weddings, the Gold Coast Farm House team will be there to ensure you have a magical and stress-free day. They are available every step of the way to answer any questions, offer suggestions, and work alongside your coordinators, no matter how big or small your celebration.


You’ll love your experience with the Gold Coast Farm House team and will cherish the wonderful memories of your magical day for years to come.

Celebrate your special day with your closest family and friends, our medium marquee welcomes up to 100 guests. Choose between an interior or exterior dance floor to dance the night away. You and your guests will have plenty of room to dance until you can’t dance any longer.

## Stunning wedding ceremony locations

With 60 acres of stunning hinterland property, Gold Coast Farm House has a wide range of beautiful ceremony locations for you to choose from! We have some gorgeous popular spots, but if you have a specific vision for your day we’re here to make it happen!

### WEDDING CEREMONY LOCATIONS

POINT OF THE LAKE

Celebrate with all your closest loved ones at the Point of the Lake. Located on the main path of the property, this location has proved to be one of the most loved of all of our wedding ceremony packages. Enjoy 360° views of the Gold Coast hinterland, with a perfect view of Page’s Pinnacle and its surrounds. This location is the ideal blank slate for all couples, with endless opportunities for decorations and style.

Keep it rustic with wooden chairs, a wooden arbour and some native blooms or go all out with luxury touches including archways and elegant floral arrangements.

With all tipis or marquees located on the opposite side of this lake, guests will get to enjoy a sneak peek of the celebrations to come. Sit all of your guests comfortably at the Point of the Lake, with ample room for the grandest of all ceremonies.

under the treEs

Find yourself lost in the wonder and whimsy of our 100-year-old tallow-wood tree with its large dignified branches and enchanting stance. Say your “I do’s” underneath its large limbs, with all of your guests watching on from the grass surrounding.

This one of a kind space is accented by a natural woven archway for the wedding party to make their entrance through, making for a stunning photo opportunity. No need to worry about extravagant floral arrangements or large works of architecture here, with the tree doing all the work.

This unique wedding ceremony package is the perfect way to establish a whimsical, fairytale feeling for your big day. Often decorated with layered bohemian rugs, mismatched chairs and candles this ceremony location makes for beautiful photos filled with texture and colour. 


With room for 150 seated guests, the point of the tree works great for weddings both intimate and grand – with the front rows covered by the shade of the tree, this stunning location is excellent year-round. Let your guests take in the glorious views of Numinbah Valley and the gorgeous Gold Coast hinterland while they eagerly await the wedding parties arrival.

THE GAZEBO

For an intimate or more understated ceremony, our Gazebo wedding ceremony package is for you. This gorgeous white timber arbour wrapped in grapevines is the ideal backdrop for you to share your vows with your closest loved ones. Don’t stress about set up or pack down with your own venue coordinator for the day to ensure everything runs without a hitch.

Overlooking the farm beyond with bubbling creeks running nearby, this serene and quaint location provides an elegant backdrop for all types of  ceremonies from weddings, elopements and vow renewals.

Cross the love lock bridge as the trees open up to reveal a large field in which all your friends and family can sit to watch you exchange your vows.

Embrace the magical ambience of the gazebo and decorate with whimsical multi-coloured blooms or keep it neutral with soft creams and beiges. Explore the 60-acre farm surrounding for your wedding portraiture while your guests only take a short walk to the cocktail and reception space.

THE PIER

Get married on the water at the pier – located on one of our three natural lakes on the property. This gorgeous timber pier over the lake makes for the ideal backdrop for all sorts of ceremonies. Located closest to the house, this wedding ceremony package allows for the longest walk to the altar, for those looking to make a dramatic entrance.

Say your vows with the gorgeous lake and rolling hills and mountains of the Gold Coast hinterland as your backdrop, making for awe-inspiring portraits.

Watch as the sun dances off the water and bounces in the large trees above to make for the most picturesque backdrop.

Seating all of your guests comfortably on the lawn, this space is often decorated with soft blooms and architectural touches to accent the pier and keep the natural, rustic and romantic feel of the space.

1628	# Dog Friendly Wedding at the Farm House
1629	
1630	Is your dog more than just a pet? Would you like to include them in your special day? At the Gold Coast Farm House we warmly welcome your pets and animals to the property. With acres of lush lawns and shady trees, your dog will have the time of their lives at our dog friendly wedding venue.
1631	
1632	There are so many wonderful ways that your dog can be involved in your wedding day. Whether they are there for moral support or you create your whole wedding theme around them, dogs are part of the family and should be included in your special day.
1633	
1634	We invite you to bring your dog out to the Farm House when you come to view the property. Simply let us know at the time of booking your viewing and we will prepare ourselves to welcome your furry friend. It will be our pleasure.
1635	
1636	## Walk down the aisle
1637	
1638	Make your pooch Dog of Honour or Best Dog, or simply have them accompany you down the aisle. Involving your beloved pet in your ceremony adds a fun and unique element to your celebration and you get to have your (other) best friend by your side.
1639	
1640	## Cute little outfits
1641	
1642	Nothing brings immense joy quite like dressing up a dog. Bow ties, flowers, tutus, or tuxedos, the options for adorning your furry friend are endless. Providing your pet is ok with it, dressing them in theme for your wedding will put smiles on the face of every guest and make yours a celebration to remember.
1643	
1644	## Ring Bearers and Flower Dogs
1645	
1646	While they say “never work with children or animals”, just choose one. Forget the kids and put your puppy to work as the ring bearer or flower dog. Get creative with pouches or boxes to keep your treasures safe as your pet delivers them to you and your love.
1647	
1648	## Dancing dogs
1649	
1650	Let your pup loose on the dance floor and have fun including your furry best friend in your festivities. First dance with your life partner? Get your pet in on the action and make it a moment you will never forget.

1653	
1654	Having an experienced photographer capture your memories is essential for every wedding. Ensuring all your loved ones are represented in your photos is paramount. This is also true for your furry friends. Dogs and other animals add a whimsical feel to your shots and often provide the most entertaining candid images for your album.
1655	
1656	Whether you include your own pet or you bring in unique animals for your special day is up to you. Your celebration will be more memorable and your photos will bring joy for years to come.
1657	
1658	## Dog theme your wedding
1659	
1660	Create your whole wedding theme around your dog. Why not? Dogs are cute and getting creative with imagery on stationery, desserts, signage, or gifts is a fun way to honour the special relationship you have with your pooch. ## Event Venue GOLD COAST

Looking for a unique event venue on the Gold Coast?

Something nearby to local attractions but still quiet and secluded, hidden away amongst the hinterland. Gold Coast Farm House is your ideal location to host birthday parties, memorial services, corporate events or fundraising events.

### EVENT OPTIONS

Our 60-acre property is located only 30 minutes from Surfers Paradise or an hour and a half from Brisbane, only a short trip away from the hustle and bustle of the city into the hidden paradise that is the Numinbah hinterlands. With three natural lakes, secret glow worm caves and running creeks you will be transported to a world of serenity, ideal for all sorts of private events.

Corporate Events

Engagement parties

Photoshoots

### Renovated Queenslander For Your Event

Make the most of our renovated Queenslander home and have a private lunch on the deck overlooking the Numinbah Hinterlands and Pages Pinnacle. Choose to hire a food truck for the day or have your own chef come and cook in the kitchen. Take your event down by the lake and enjoy stunning views of native flora and fauna while you celebrate.

### Corporate events

Host your corporate event out at the farm house, with ample room for activities and electricity running through all key locations on the property. Enjoy lunch on the deck and then make your way down to the jetty for motivational talks or to play games. Our acres of lush green lawns are perfect for team building activities or team sports.

### Engagement Parties & More

Have your big events at our outdoor venue on the Gold Coast. Perfect for engagement parties and corporate functions. With sweeping landscapes, stunning views, and plenty of room for activities, your party will have guests talking for years to come. Hire our tipi packages for a large event complete with a portable bathroom and furniture hire or DIY it to suit your own personal style.

### Private Photoshoots

Our venue is perfect for private photoshoots including engagement shoots, fashion shoots or portraiture. We have ample room and locations that will make for stunning photos – like the point of the lake, the jetty and our newly renovated Queenslander home. For all photoshoot enquiries please enquire via our contact email bookings@goldcoastfarmhouse.com.au

#### FAQ's

#### What kind of event can I have at The Farm?

The Farm is suitable for corporate parties like lunches, launch parties, motivational talks, and team building activities.

We also host Celebration of Life to celebrate your loved ones.

Other events that are perfect for the farm are: engagement parties, bridal showers, gender reveals, private photo shoots, and more!

#### How Many People Can I Have?

Our 60 acre property can host a large amount of people. For large events, we suggest hiring a tipi with a portable bathroom to use.

#### What Food Options Are There?

Up to you! We have a few food & drink recommendations, but ultimately it’s your choice.

# Dog Friendly Wedding at the Farm House

Is your dog more than just a pet? Would you like to include them in your special day? At the Gold Coast Farm House we warmly welcome your pets and animals to the property. With acres of lush lawns and shady trees, your dog will have the time of their lives at our dog friendly wedding venue.

There are so many wonderful ways that your dog can be involved in your wedding day. Whether they are there for moral support or you create your whole wedding theme around them, dogs are part of the family and should be included in your special day.

We invite you to bring your dog out to the Farm House when you come to view the property. Simply let us know at the time of booking your viewing and we will prepare ourselves to welcome your furry friend. It will be our pleasure.

## Walk down the aisle

Make your pooch Dog of Honour or Best Dog, or simply have them accompany you down the aisle. Involving your beloved pet in your ceremony adds a fun and unique element to your celebration and you get to have your (other) best friend by your side.

## Cute little outfits

Nothing brings immense joy quite like dressing up a dog. Bow ties, flowers, tutus, or tuxedos, the options for adorning your furry friend are endless. Providing your pet is ok with it, dressing them in theme for your wedding will put smiles on the face of every guest and make yours a celebration to remember.

## Ring Bearers and Flower Dogs

While they say “never work with children or animals”, just choose one. Forget the kids and put your puppy to work as the ring bearer or flower dog. Get creative with pouches or boxes to keep your treasures safe as your pet delivers them to you and your love.

## Dancing dogs

Let your pup loose on the dance floor and have fun including your furry best friend in your festivities. First dance with your life partner? Get your pet in on the action and make it a moment you will never forget.

## Include them in photos

Having an experienced photographer capture your memories is essential for every wedding. Ensuring all your loved ones are represented in your photos is paramount. This is also true for your furry friends. Dogs and other animals add a whimsical feel to your shots and often provide the most entertaining candid images for your album.

Whether you include your own pet or you bring in unique animals for your special day is up to you. Your celebration will be more memorable and your photos will bring joy for years to come.

## Dog theme your wedding

Create your whole wedding theme around your dog. Why not? Dogs are cute and getting creative with imagery on stationery, desserts, signage, or gifts is a fun way to honour the special relationship you have with your pooch. Keep it subtle or go all out and express to your guests just how important your four-legged friend is to you.

## Other pets and animals

Is your best furry friend a cat? Bring them along! All fluffy family members are welcome. Surprise your beloved like one our beautiful brides did, as she walked her groom’s best feline friend down the aisle, carrying their rings (See above for the very special moment between the two). Animals are deeply loved and treasured that they deserve to be present in your most important life moments.

The Gold Coast Farm House has welcomed all kinds of animals over the years, with some of the most memorable being alpacas from local farms. Cute farm animals are also lovely to have at your wedding with our wide open spaces making the perfect location for furry and feathered friends.

1980	
1981	Valentine’s Day has always been about love – but this year, it came with a ring.

2000	- Are we drawn to relaxed, countryside charm or something more formal?
2001	- What moments matter most to us – vows, food, dancing, family time?

2006	
2007	It may not feel very Valentine’s Day–romantic, but having an honest budget conversation early on is one of the kindest things you can do for yourselves.

2009	Think of your budget as a guide – it helps you focus on what truly matters and choose vendors and venues that align with your priorities. Many couples find that choosing a venue like the Gold Coast Farm House, where the setting itself creates so much atmosphere, allows them to simplify other decisions.

2011	### Choose Your Date (or Your Season)
2012	
2013	Some couples are attached to a meaningful date, while others fall in love with a season. There’s no wrong choice – just what feels right for you.

2015	Dreaming of long summer evenings, golden sunsets, and outdoor celebrations? Or maybe you love the idea of a softer autumn light, candlelit dinners, and cozy country romance. The Gold Coast Farm House offers beautiful backdrops year-round, making it easier to choose a date that suits your vision.
2016	
2017	### Find a Venue That Feels Like Home
2018	
2019	Your venue sets the tone for your entire wedding day. It’s where your guests will gather, where your story will unfold, and where memories will be made.
2020	
2021	When you visit a venue, notice how it *feels*:
2022	
2023	- Can you picture yourselves exchanging vows here?
2024	- Does it feel welcoming and relaxed?
2025	- Does it reflect your style and values?
2026	
2027	Couples often tell us that the Gold Coast Farm House feels like stepping into a place where time slows down – a space that’s elegant yet comfortable, refined yet full of heart. That feeling matters.
2028	
2029	### Enjoy the Journey

2031	Wedding planning isn’t just about the final day – it’s about the journey you take together to get there. There will be decisions, laughter, moments of “does this really matter?”, and so much excitement along the way.

2127	# How to Host a Dry Wedding
2128	
2129	## Planning a Dry Wedding or Low-Alcohol Celebration? You’re Not Alone.
2130	
2131	There’s a growing shift in the world of weddings, and we are here for it. More and more couples are saying *“cheers!”* with sparkling water, mocktails, or zero alcohol champagne. Whether it’s for personal preference, cultural reasons, health, budget, or just a vibe, you don’t *need* alcohol to have an incredible, joy-filled wedding day.
2132	
2133	At Gold Coast Farm House, we’ve seen first-hand how dry weddings (or low-alcohol celebrations) can be just as fun, meaningful, and memorable as any party with a bar tab. The best part? Our venue is totally flexible, so you can create the experience that feels right for you.
2134	
2135	### Why Couples Are Choosing Dry or Low-Alcohol Weddings
2136	
2137	There are plenty of reasons why couples are skipping the booze or scaling it way back, including:
2138	
2139	- Personal or religious beliefs
2140	- Health and wellness goals
2141	- Budget-conscious planning
2142	- A guest list that includes kids or teens
2143	- Sober guests who deserve to feel fully included
2144	- Wanting a clear head to fully soak in the day!
2145	
2146	And sometimes, it’s as simple as *“we just don’t drink much and don’t feel like we need it.”* Love that!
2147	
2148	### What a Dry Wedding Can Look Like at Gold Coast Farm House
2149	
2150	The great thing about our venue? You have complete control over your drinks menu. You can provide your own alcohol – you just need RSA-certified bar staff to serve it responsibly. For dry or low-alcohol weddings, the options are still endless.
2151	
2152	#### A few ways we’ve seen it done:
2153	
2154	- **Self- served or staffed non-alcoholic bar setups** serving iced teas, lemonade, sparkling waters, or kombucha
2155	- **Mocktail menus** served by a licensed mobile bar
2156	- **Non-alcoholic beer, wine, and spirits** displayed beautifully and served by staff or self-served
2157	- **Champagne-style towers** using non-alcoholic sparkling wine for a toast
2158	- **Kombucha or specialty soda bars** run by vendors or friends
2159	
2160	Just because you’re skipping the booze doesn’t mean you can’t still have a beautiful drinks experience.
2161	
2162	### Bonus: You’ll Save Big on Your Bar Budget
2163	
2164	Let’s be honest, alcohol can take a big slice out of the wedding budget pie. A dry or low-alcohol wedding often means:
2165	
2166	- Less spent on alcohol purchases
2167	- Fewer bar staff hours needed
2168	- Lower glassware and bar hire costs
2169	- Less waste and post-party cleanup
2170	- You’re also most likely to get your bus bond back as there will be much less chance of guests feeling unwell on the drive home.
2171	
2172	All that extra room in your budget? Spend it on florals, food, entertainment or that killer acoustic duo you’ve had your eye on.
2173	
2174	### But… Will People Still Have Fun?
2175	
2176	Short answer: Absolutely!
2177	
2178	We’ve hosted dry weddings where guests danced all night, played lawn games at sunset, laughed until they cried, and made the most of every moment. When the energy is good, the planning is thoughtful, and the love is strong – you don’t need a full bar to have a full heart.
2179	
2180	### A few fun additions that keep the party rolling:
2181	
2182	- Live band or DJ with interactive sets
2183	- Lawn games and mingling spaces
2184	- Coffee cart or late-night dessert truck
2185	- A sparkler send-off or acoustic circle around the firepit
2186	- A sunset ceremony followed by a twilight garden party
2187	
2188	### Not Fully Dry? Try a Low-Alcohol Hybrid
2189	
2190	Some couples opt for a low-alcohol approach instead of going fully dry. For example:
2191	
2192	- A champagne toast only
2193	- One signature cocktail alongside non-alcoholic versions
2194	- Beer and wine only, served during limited hours
2195	- A full bar- but with a heavy focus on non-alcoholic options
2196	
2197	Because Gold Coast Farm House is a BYO-friendly venue, you can bring your own alcohol and work with an RSA-certified vendor or mobile bar to serve it—your way, legally and responsibly.
2198	
2199	### At the End of the Day, It’s About You
2200	
2201	There are no rules anymore. Your wedding should reflect your values, your preferences, and your lifestyle. If that means no alcohol – *amazing*. If that means just a splash of bubbly at golden hour- *perfect*.
2202	
2203	At Gold Coast Farm House, we’re here to support whatever vision you have – dry, low-alcohol, or full bar fiesta. Either way, it’s going to be unforgettable.
2204

2207	Let’s make it magic – *your way.*

# You’re Engaged! Now What?

## Your First Steps to Planning the Wedding of Your Dreams

Valentine’s Day has always been about love – but this year, it came with a ring. 

If you’re newly engaged (congratulations!), you might be floating on cloud nine… while also quietly wondering, *“Okay, now what do we actually do?”*

Take a deep breath. Wedding planning doesn’t have to feel overwhelming. In fact, the very first steps should feel exciting, intentional, and, most importantly, *yours*. Here’s how to begin planning your wedding in a way that sets the tone for everything that comes next.

### Pause & Celebrate This Season

Before diving into spreadsheets and Pinterest boards, give yourselves permission to just *be engaged*. Go out for a Valentine’s dinner, pop a bottle of champagne at home, or take a quiet walk together and soak it all in.

This season is short and sweet, so don’t rush past it. The best weddings begin with couples who truly enjoy this moment together.

### Dream Together Before Making Decisions

Before booking anything, sit down and talk about what you both imagine for your day.

Ask each other:

- Do we want something intimate or a big celebration?
- Are we drawn to relaxed, countryside charm or something more formal?
- What moments matter most to us – vows, food, dancing, family time?

At the Gold Coast Farm House, we often see couples fall in love with the idea of a wedding that feels personal, warm, and effortlessly beautiful – where guests feel at home and every moment feels unhurried. Finding that shared vision early makes planning feel exciting instead of overwhelming.

### Set a Comfortable Budget (Yes, Even Now)

It may not feel very Valentine’s Day–romantic, but having an honest budget conversation early on is one of the kindest things you can do for yourselves.

Think of your budget as a guide – it helps you focus on what truly matters and choose vendors and venues that align with your priorities. Many couples find that choosing a venue like the Gold Coast Farm House, where the setting itself creates so much atmosphere, allows them to simplify other decisions.

### Choose Your Date (or Your Season)

Some couples are attached to a meaningful date, while others fall in love with a season. There’s no wrong choice – just what feels right for you.

Dreaming of long summer evenings, golden sunsets, and outdoor celebrations? Or maybe you love the idea of a softer autumn light, candlelit dinners, and cozy country romance. The Gold Coast Farm House offers beautiful backdrops year-round, making it easier to choose a date that suits your vision.

### Find a Venue That Feels Like Home

Your venue sets the tone for your entire wedding day. It’s where your guests will gather, where your story will unfold, and where memories will be made.

When you visit a venue, notice how it *feels*:

- Can you picture yourselves exchanging vows here?
- Does it feel welcoming and relaxed?
- Does it reflect your style and values?

Couples often tell us that the Gold Coast Farm House feels like stepping into a place where time slows down – a space that’s elegant yet comfortable, refined yet full of heart. That feeling matters.

### Enjoy the Journey

Wedding planning isn’t just about the final day – it’s about the journey you take together to get there. There will be decisions, laughter, moments of “does this really matter?”, and so much excitement along the way.

This Valentine’s Day marks the beginning of that journey. Wherever you choose to celebrate, let your wedding planning start the same way your engagement did – with love, intention, and a little magic.

# How to Host a Dry Wedding

## Planning a Dry Wedding or Low-Alcohol Celebration? You’re Not Alone.

There’s a growing shift in the world of weddings, and we are here for it. More and more couples are saying *“cheers!”* with sparkling water, mocktails, or zero alcohol champagne. Whether it’s for personal preference, cultural reasons, health, budget, or just a vibe, you don’t *need* alcohol to have an incredible, joy-filled wedding day.

At Gold Coast Farm House, we’ve seen first-hand how dry weddings (or low-alcohol celebrations) can be just as fun, meaningful, and memorable as any party with a bar tab. The best part? Our venue is totally flexible, so you can create the experience that feels right for you.

### Why Couples Are Choosing Dry or Low-Alcohol Weddings

There are plenty of reasons why couples are skipping the booze or scaling it way back, including:

- Personal or religious beliefs
- Health and wellness goals
- Budget-conscious planning
- A guest list that includes kids or teens
- Sober guests who deserve to feel fully included
- Wanting a clear head to fully soak in the day!

And sometimes, it’s as simple as *“we just don’t drink much and don’t feel like we need it.”* Love that!

### What a Dry Wedding Can Look Like at Gold Coast Farm House

The great thing about our venue? You have complete control over your drinks menu. You can provide your own alcohol – you just need RSA-certified bar staff to serve it responsibly. For dry or low-alcohol weddings, the options are still endless.

#### A few ways we’ve seen it done:

- **Self- served or staffed non-alcoholic bar setups** serving iced teas, lemonade, sparkling waters, or kombucha
- **Mocktail menus** served by a licensed mobile bar
- **Non-alcoholic beer, wine, and spirits** displayed beautifully and served by staff or self-served
- **Champagne-style towers** using non-alcoholic sparkling wine for a toast
- **Kombucha or specialty soda bars** run by vendors or friends

Just because you’re skipping the booze doesn’t mean you can’t still have a beautiful drinks experience.

### Bonus: You’ll Save Big on Your Bar Budget

Let’s be honest, alcohol can take a big slice out of the wedding budget pie. A dry or low-alcohol wedding often means:

- Less spent on alcohol purchases
- Fewer bar staff hours needed
- Lower glassware and bar hire costs
- Less waste and post-party cleanup
- You’re also most likely to get your bus bond back as there will be much less chance of guests feeling unwell on the drive home.

All that extra room in your budget? Spend it on florals, food, entertainment or that killer acoustic duo you’ve had your eye on.

### But… Will People Still Have Fun?

Short answer: Absolutely!

We’ve hosted dry weddings where guests danced all night, played lawn games at sunset, laughed until they cried, and made the most of every moment. When the energy is good, the planning is thoughtful, and the love is strong – you don’t need a full bar to have a full heart.

### A few fun additions that keep the party rolling:

- Live band or DJ with interactive sets
- Lawn games and mingling spaces
- Coffee cart or late-night dessert truck
- A sparkler send-off or acoustic circle around the firepit
- A sunset ceremony followed by a twilight garden party

### Not Fully Dry? Try a Low-Alcohol Hybrid

Some couples opt for a low-alcohol approach instead of going fully dry. For example:

- A champagne toast only
- One signature cocktail alongside non-alcoholic versions
- Beer and wine only, served during limited hours
- A full bar- but with a heavy focus on non-alcoholic options

Because Gold Coast Farm House is a BYO-friendly venue, you can bring your own alcohol and work with an RSA-certified vendor or mobile bar to serve it—your way, legally and responsibly.

### At the End of the Day, It’s About You

There are no rules anymore. Your wedding should reflect your values, your preferences, and your lifestyle. If that means no alcohol – *amazing*. If that means just a splash of bubbly at golden hour- *perfect*.

At Gold Coast Farm House, we’re here to support whatever vision you have – dry, low-alcohol, or full bar fiesta. Either way, it’s going to be unforgettable.

#### Planning a dry or low-alcohol wedding in the Gold Coast Hinterland?

Let’s make it magic – *your way.*

Contact us to book a viewing or ask about drinks service options that fit your celebration.

# Wedding Pet Portraits

It’s no secret that we love dogs here at the Gold Coast Farm House, and back in May, we were treated to not one, but two, gorgeous pooches. Caitlin and Joel tied the knot in a stunning and intimate ceremony at the point of the lake with their best friends playing a pivotal role in their big day. After helping Caitlin get ready at the Farm House, the Spoodle and Australian Shepherd were lead to the ceremony by the bridesmaids, greeting the couple with enthusiastic kisses and wagging tails. The furry pair then watched from their designated grassy seats as Mum and Dad declared their love for each other.

The lucky pups were finally allowed to roam free on the property, but not before congratulating Caitlin and Joel at the signing table. Walks along the winding country path, a ride on the buggy, and a free range run through the fields followed. The dogs were having a memorable day of their own while the newly weds took in every special new moment together as husband and wife.

Dressed in their adorable doggy pyjamas, the pooches joined in the intimate reception on the deck of the Farm House with plenty of treats, cuddles, and the occasional game of chasey. Brittany from Wallflower Weddings captured so many precious moments with the newly weds and their fur babies, resulting in a stunning wedding album for Caitlin and Joel to treasure forever. We hope you enjoy these beautiful images as they inspire your future wedding pet portraits at the Gold Coast Farm House.


## PAGE [wedding]: https://goldcoastfarmhouse.com.au/about-us/

## Our Venue

Gold Coast Farm House is situated in the beautiful Numinbah Valley, just 30 km from Surfers Paradise. With 60 acres of rolling lush green grass lawn spotted with large native trees, 2 large spring fed dam’s and surrounded by national park, it’s the perfect location for a private wedding or function.


Tony’s Creek runs the full length of the property with 3 swimming holes, a secret glow worm cave and some small waterfalls, there are multiple bush walks starting from the property for you to explore. Alternatively, just sit back, relax and enjoy watching the native bird life in the trees and wallaby’s grazing .


The 100 plus year-old Queenslander sits at the top of the property overlooking the dams and has an uninterrupted view of Springbrook National Park and Page’s Pinnacle. With its high ceilings and beautiful leadlight windows, it truly feels like you have stepped back in time.

The large deck can hold up to 40 people seated for an intimate wedding or a large family gathering. We have 4 different wedding ceremony locations to choose from – point of the dam, jetty over the dam, gazebo and under our beautiful 100 year old tree.

Our marquee or tipi site is large and level, beautifully positioned next to our dam and can accommodate up to 150 guests depending on the number of tipis you choose or the size of your marquee.

Gold Coast Farm House is private and secluded, your guests will be so surprised when they come down the driveway and around the corner and look out across the dam and your beautiful reception.

The Farm House is the passion project of Gold Coast locals, Marcia and Jeff. With a flair for creativity and design, the pair were able to envisage the property’s potential, showcasing the natural surrounds and the classic Queenslander home.


Their experience with interior design and love for all things vintage led them to lovingly restore and transform the vast rural space into a stunning country wedding venue.


Originally bought as a family property, the Farm House quickly evolved into a wedding venue with requests for a unique and beautiful location for celebrations. The innovative pair jumped at the chance to share their stunning homestead with loved up couples for their special day.


Their successful creative enterprises keep them close to central Gold Coast business districts, however their dream is to retire to the Farm House to spend their days tending to the magical Hinterland property and living the idyllic country lifestyle.

While Marcia and Jeff are still very hands-on with maintaining and enhancing the property, they have handed over bookings and venue coordination to the wider Farm House team. Experienced and approachable, the team works closely with couples and wedding planners to ensure every detail is perfectly organised for a seamless ceremony and reception.


Well versed in weddings, the Gold Coast Farm House team will be there to ensure you have a magical and stress-free day. They are available every step of the way to answer any questions, offer suggestions, and work alongside your coordinators, no matter how big or small your celebration.


You’ll love your experience with the Gold Coast Farm House team and will cherish the wonderful memories of your magical day for years to come.

6716	## PAGE [wedding]: https://goldcoastfarmhouse.com.au/blog/page/12/
6717	
6718	### 2021 Wedding Venue Trends
6719	
6720	If you’re in the process of planning your wedding and are looking for some inspiration, we’ve compiled a list of wedding venue trends for you to take a look at!
6721	
6722	### Elle & Scott’s Wedding
6723	
6724	Elle and Scott chose this Gold Coast wedding venue nestled in beautiful Numibah Valley to share with their friends and family. Numinbah Valley is part of the Gold Coast Hinterland and Scenic Rim region surrounded by heritage listed national parks.
6725	
6726	### Lauryn and Luke’s Wedding
6727	
6728	No wedding will ever be the same as Lauren and Luke’s was at the Gold Coast Farm House, complete with Llama’s for guests to pat. This Gold Coast wedding venue has plenty of room to set up your dream wedding, bring your pets and even have a game of crochet. Lauren wanted to DIY as much of her wedding as possible. She made her own floral arrangements for her arbor, bridesmaids and herself. Instead of buying a wedding cake she instead opted for donuts, simple, cheap and easy but delicious all the same.
6729	
6730	
6731	## PAGE [wedding]: https://goldcoastfarmhouse.com.au/dog-friendly-wedding-at-the-farm-house/
6732	
6733	# Dog Friendly Wedding at the Farm House
6734	
6735	Is your dog more than just a pet? Would you like to include them in your special day? At the Gold Coast Farm House we warmly welcome your pets and animals to the property. With acres of lush lawns and shady trees, your dog will have the time of their lives at our dog friendly wedding venue.
6736	
6737	There are so many wonderful ways that your dog can be involved in your wedding day. Whether they are there for moral support or you create your whole wedding theme around them, dogs are part of the family and should be included in your special day.
6738	
6739	We invite you to bring your dog out to the Farm House when you come to view the property. Simply let us know at the time of booking your viewing and we will prepare ourselves to welcome your furry friend. It will be our pleasure.
6740	
6741	## Walk down the aisle
6742	
6743	Make your pooch Dog of Honour or Best Dog, or simply have them accompany you down the aisle. Involving your beloved pet in your ceremony adds a fun and unique element to your celebration and you get to have your (other) best friend by your side.
6744	
6745	## Cute little outfits
6746	
6747	Nothing brings immense joy quite like dressing up a dog. Bow ties, flowers, tutus, or tuxedos, the options for adorning your furry friend are endless. Providing your pet is ok with it, dressing them in theme for your wedding will put smiles on the face of every guest and make yours a celebration to remember.
6748	
6749	## Ring Bearers and Flower Dogs
6750	
6751	While they say “never work with children or animals”, just choose one. Forget the kids and put your puppy to work as the ring bearer or flower dog. Get creative with pouches or boxes to keep your treasures safe as your pet delivers them to you and your love.
6752	
6753	## Dancing dogs
6754	
6755	Let your pup loose on the dance floor and have fun including your furry best friend in your festivities. First dance with your life partner? Get your pet in on the action and make it a moment you will never forget.
6756	
6757	## Include them in photos
6758	
6759	Having an experienced photographer capture your memories is essential for every wedding. Ensuring all your loved ones are represented in your photos is paramount. This is also true for your furry friends. Dogs and other animals add a whimsical feel to your shots and often provide the most entertaining candid images for your album.
6760	
6761	Whether you include your own pet or you bring in unique animals for your special day is up to you. Your celebration will be more memorable and your photos will bring joy for years to come.
6762	
6763	## Dog theme your wedding
6764	
6765	Create your whole wedding theme around your dog. Why not? Dogs are cute and getting creative with imagery on stationery, desserts, signage, or gifts is a fun way to honour the special relationship you have with your pooch. Keep it subtle or go all out and express to your guests just how important your four-legged friend is to you.
6766	
6767	## Other pets and animals
6768	
6769	Is your best furry friend a cat? Bring them along! All fluffy family members are welcome. Surprise your beloved like one our beautiful brides did, as she walked her groom’s best feline friend down the aisle, carrying their rings (See above for the very special moment between the two). Animals are deeply loved and treasured that they deserve to be present in your most important life moments.
6770	
6771	The Gold Coast Farm House has welcomed all kinds of animals over the years, with some of the most memorable being alpacas from local farms. Cute farm animals are also lovely to have at your wedding with our wide open spaces making the perfect location for furry and feathered friends.
6772	
6773	
6774	## PAGE [wedding]: https://goldcoastfarmhouse.com.au/
6775	
6776	## Our Wedding Packages
6777	
6778	We have a variety of wedding packages to suit all budgets and sizing for your big day!
6779	
6780	## CHECK YOUR DATES
6781	
6782	Check if your desired dates are available on our calendar and get in touch to organise a viewing.
6783	
6784	## BOOK YOUR WEDDING
6785	
6786	Contact our owners to secure your Gold Coast Farm House wedding or event!
6787	
6788	### GOLD COAST HINTERLAND
6789	
6790	We’re located in the Numinbah Valley, surrounded by national park. If you’ve been dreaming of a wedding in the hinterland at more well known locations like Mount Tamborine, our nearby property will likely blow your mind with it’s glistening creek and spectacular views!
6791	
6792	### WEDDING CEREMONY OPTIONS
6793	
6794	Choose from a range of gorgeous locations to have your ceremony – from ancient trees, to picturesque dams with lily pads and ivy covered gazebos (keep scrolling to see photos). Style the ceremony your way – choose from our included arbors or bring your own.
6795	
6796	### Intimate weddings
6797	
6798	Our large undercover deck can be styled beautifully, and will seat up to 40 people for a small, intimate wedding option. The view of our two dams, the countryside and Page’s Pinnacle from the deck will take your breath away.
6799	
6800	### WEDDING RECEPTION OPTIONS
6801	
6802	If you’re planning a bigger outdoor wedding, choose a tipi or marquee package for your rainforest surrounded reception. Our tipis bring a fun festival vibe, and our marquees are a glamourous garden party option.
6803	
6804	### PET FRIENDLY VENUE
6805	
6806	We get it, your pets are your family – of course they should be a part of your big day! Incorporate your fur babies into your ceremony and reception however you see fit. Read our wedding blogs from our dog friendly venue.
6807	
6808	### Cater your way
6809	
6810	It’s your day – you should eat your favourite food and drink your favourite wine! Our BYO wedding venue is completely self-catered. Host the wedding of your dreams with your own caterers and BYO bar and beverages.
6811	
6812	### OUTDOOR WEDDING MAGIC
6813	
6814	Have you been fantasising about a wedding surrounded by nature? Get married amongst the rainforest and under the stars at our Gold Coast Hinterland property.
6815	
6816	We’re only a 45 minute drive from Surfers Paradise, and an hour and a half from Brisbane, but you’ll feel like you’re in another world.
6817
